> 小國寡民。使有什伯之器而不用.

This is the most argued-over chapter in the book. Those who attack it say it wants a return to the primitive; those who praise it say it is the first utopia. Both read it fast.

The weight is not in 小 and 寡. It is in six 使 and one 復.

## Six 使, and none of them removes anything

使有什伯之器而不用 — has the equipment of ten or a hundred, and does not use it.
使民重死而不遠徙 — the people take death heavily and do not move far away.
雖有舟輿，無所乘之 — there are boats and carts, and nowhere they are taken.
雖有甲兵，無所陳之 — there is armor and arms, and nowhere they are deployed.
使民復結繩而用之 — the people return to knotted cords and use them.

Every one of the six is have-and-do-not-start. Nothing is taken away. The vessels exist; the ships exist; the weapons exist. What does not exist is the occasion.

## 復 is a return, and 結繩 has an opponent

Return to what? To knotted cords.

And knotted cords have an exact opponent — 《周易·系辭下》: 上古結繩而治，後世聖人易之以書契.

Cords were replaced by 書契. And 契 is chapter 79's split tally.

So the order of these two chapters is deliberate: 79 shows a man holding half a notched piece of wood; 80 has everyone go back to the knot.

Laozi is not sending anyone back to the primitive. He is having them put down the half.

## 重死

重死 is the same 重 as chapter 75's 求生之厚 — weight, and the word is used in the opposite direction here.

The people take death as heavy, therefore they do not migrate far. Not because travel is forbidden: because life has enough weight in it that leaving costs something.

And 甘其食，美其服，安其居，樂其俗 — each of the four is 其: their own. Their food is sweet, their clothes are fine, their dwelling is settled, their customs are a joy.

Note where 美 appears: 美其服. Chapter 81 will say that of the eight occurrences of 美 in the book, seven are a disease and this one passes. It passes because the subject is the person wearing the clothes.

## 鄰國相望，雞犬之聲相聞，民至老死，不相往來

Neighboring states see each other; the cocks and dogs hear each other; the people reach old age and death without coming and going.

This is the line that gets read as isolation. Read with the six 使, it is the absence of occasion: nothing needs to be brought from there, and nothing needs to be sent. Two households close enough to hear each other's animals, and no reason to move.

## Why this follows 79

79: do not keep the tally.
80: and a people who no longer need to travel to settle accounts.

The whole chapter is one subtraction at the level of a community: what disappears is not comfort, not tools, not contact — it is the compulsion to go and get something from someone else.

## A test

Take the last three journeys you made — the ones with a purpose. Ask what you went to obtain. Most of them will have been to collect something that was owed, or to press a claim. That is the half-wood being walked across a border.
